title: Sikerült Megoldanom: Solving It, and Telling the Story

sections.title: From problem to story
sections.content: Once you've explained what's wrong, Hungarian gives you a clean way to finish the story: hívtam ("I called") someone, they eljött ("came over") and megjavította ("fixed it", the definite past you already know from megoldta). sikerült ("it succeeded, it worked out") behaves just like kell and lehet — it never changes for person — and pairs with the personal infinitive ending from kell dolgoznom: sikerült megoldanom means literally "it succeeded for-me to-solve", i.e. "I managed to solve it".

sections.title: Solving it, and saying so
rows: He/she came over, and fixed the washing machine.
I managed to solve the problem.
In the end everything turned out fine.

items.spanish: Tegnap elromlott a zuhany, ezért hívtam egy szerelőt.
items.english: Yesterday the shower broke, so I called a repairman.

items.spanish: Gyorsan eljött, és fél óra alatt megjavította.
items.english: He came quickly, and fixed it within half an hour.

items.spanish: Nagyon büszke voltam, hogy egyedül, magyarul sikerült mindent megoldanom.
items.english: I was very proud that I managed to solve everything by myself, in Hungarian.

sections.content: sikerült stays exactly the same no matter who managed it — only the infinitive changes, with the same -nom/-nod/-nia endings kell dolgoznom already taught you: sikerült megoldanom (I managed), sikerült megoldanod (you managed), sikerült megoldania (he/she managed).
